title: Add transactional downgrade guard, backup/restore, schema migrations and version pinning to private-installer
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds transactional downgrade guard that prevents cluster from being downgraded across incompatible schema versions.
Introduces pre-upgrade backup hooks and post-upgrade verification for DB and object storage state.
Pins component charts and terraform modules during upgrade to ensure deterministic rollouts.
body: Summary: This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to the private-installer to make upgrades and rollbacks safe and deterministic for on-prem / VPC deployments. It adds a transactional downgrade guard (prevents downgrade if schema or data state would be incompatible), integrates backup/restore hooks into the Helm/Terraform flows, makes schema migrations transactional where possible, and adds version pinning for critical components during upgrades so that rollouts can be reproduced and rolled back safely. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private require strong guarantees during upgrades to avoid data loss or irreversible schema states. Previous incidents (internal postmortem ENG-2147) showed a race between migration and rollback that could leave clusters in an unrecoverable state. This PR codifies a few guardrails: - Version pinning: the installer now supports pinning exact chart and module versions for each upgrade step. This prevents a moving target during multi-step upgrades and provides a deterministic artifact list for rollback. - Backup/restore hooks: pre-upgrade hooks will take consistent DB backups (Postgres dump + WAL capture) and snapshot object storage where configured. Post-upgrade verification runs sanity checks and optional data integrity verification. - Transactional schema migrations: database migrations are now grouped into transactional batches and use a migration coordinator that will abort the upgrade and trigger an automatic restore if a step fails. - Downgrade guard: added guard logic that refuses a downgrade if data/schema versions are newer than the target and no rollback snapshot is available. If snapshots exist, a guided restore path is advertised in the installer output. - Terraform/Helm integration: terraform module changes ensure stateful resources are not destroyed during upgrades; Helm charts implement pre/post hooks and a new values schema to enable version pinning and backup behaviour. Checklist: - [x] Add migration coordinator and transactional batcher - [x] Add pre-upgrade backup and WAL capture hooks - [x] Add post-upgrade verification and optional checksum validation - [x] Expose version pinning config in installer values and terraform module - [x] Add downgrade guard and guided restore messaging - [x] Add unit and integration tests for coordinator and hooks - [x] Update docs and release notes Backwards compatibility and upgrade path: The new values are optional and default to the previous behavior (no forced pinning, no automatic backups). Existing clusters will upgrade to the new installer with no forced changes to values; operators are encouraged to enable backups and pinning before performing major-version upgrades. If an operator attempts a manual downgrade without snapshots, the installer will block with clear instructions. Testing performed: - Unit tests for migration coordinator and guard logic (added) - Local integration tests using kind + postgres (migration + rollback flows) - Full e2e upgrade canary run in perf-canary environment with a seeded dataset (passed) - Manual validation of terraform plan to ensure no destructive actions on stateful resources - Ran helm-lint and terraform fmt/tflint/validate on changed modules Security and safety notes: Backups are stored using the cluster's configured object storage settings; no new credentials are introduced. Pre-upgrade hooks will warn if object storage is not configured and fail the upgrade if the operator enabled 'require_backups' mode. Rollback path: If an upgrade fails mid-migration, the coordinator will trigger an automatic restore if backups are available; otherwise it will stop and print step-by-step recovery instructions and contact info for SRE. Related: ENG-2147 (postmortem), ENG-2150 (upgrade playbook), SUP-4821 (customer case).

review_comments: Liam Chen (2026-02-21): Please add more unit coverage around failure modes when WAL capture misses segments. Suggest adding a test that simulates missing WAL and ensures coordinator aborts cleanly.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-22): Added unit test that simulates missing WAL and checks abort path; included documented operator message in docs. See commit d4e5f6a.
Sofia Patel (2026-02-23): Can we make "require_backups" opt-in and default to false? We should avoid breaking installs without configured object storage.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-23): "require_backups" is opt-in; default remains false. I updated values.schema and docs to clarify behavior.
Marcus Green (2026-02-24): Integration tests look good. One nit: restore-helper.sh should exit non-zero on checksum mismatch so helm hooks fail the release. Please update.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-24): Fixed exit codes in restore-helper.sh and added an integration case that validates failure on checksum mismatch.
Marcus Green (2026-02-26): Approving after e2e canary results and CI green.
